**`DB` (i.e. `postgres.DB`) — `store/db/postgres/postgres.go`**

It's declared at line 16 and holds the `*sql.DB` handle plus the profile:

```16:19:store/db/postgres/postgres.go
type DB struct {
	db      *sql.DB
	profile *profile.Profile
}
```

`NewDB` in the same file opens the connection with the `lib/pq` driver and returns `&DB{...}` as a `store.Driver`, which is how it satisfies the shared driver interface:

```33:36:store/db/postgres/postgres.go
	var driver store.Driver = &DB{
		db:      db,
		profile: profile,
	}
```

The rest of the `store.Driver` methods are implemented as `*DB` receivers across the sibling files in that package (`memo.go`, `user.go`, `attachment.go`, and so on). The MySQL and SQLite packages follow the same convention, each defining their own `DB` struct, so the type name is only unambiguous when qualified by package.
